correctness.rationale: For each d>=1 nondegenerate simplex the affine barycentric inequalities x±(W/2)u∈S are exactly λ_i(x)>=(W/2)|<g_i,u>|. Their sum A<1 makes the full feasible polytope a translate c_u+(1-A)S, not just a containing subset. Since ∑g_i=0, ∑|<g_i,u>|=2max_I<G_I,u>. The polar of the difference body C=S-S is exactly conv{G_I}: each subset-gradient satisfies the vertex-difference inequalities, and conversely any y with max_j<y,v_j>-min_k<y,v_k><=1 equals ∑_i s_i g_i with s_i∈[0,1]. Thus max_I||G_I|| is the radius of C° and equals 1/min_{||u||=1}h_C(u)=1/w(S). It follows A<=W/w(S)<1, the minimized erosion volume is (1-W/w(S))^d vol(S), and every maximizing direction is ±G_I/||G_I|| with ||G_I||=1/w. For j∈I,k∉I, <G_I,v_j-v_k>=1, so the maximizing direction places complementary vertex faces on supports separated by w. The regular-simplex Gram formula ||G_I||²=d|I|(d+1-|I|)/(d+1)² for unit-radius vertices gives balanced partitions; that regular-width subresult was previously known. The theorem does not establish single-plank attainment in dimensions >=3.
residual_risks: Finite numerical sanity tests have no bearing on the validity of universal d-dimensional identities; proof is analytic.
The theorem says nothing about optimality of one plank for high-dimensional simplices or W>w(S).
The regular-simplex width/minimizer result is established prior art; novelty must rest on full erosion computation for arbitrary simplex.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge narrower novelty: explicit exact centered-segment erosion of every simplex, identity of its directionally minimized volume with the Bang homothetic-core volume, and full complementary-face minimizer description. Prior Bakaev–Polyanskii supply a general inclusion and special-altitude plank attainment; Har-Peled–Robson (and cited older sources) already give regular-simplex minimum width and balanced optimizers. The latter regular case and the polar inradius reciprocity are not credited as novel. The Resultary pyramid result gives a width criterion without eroded-simplex minimization. No inspected prior theorem states or implies the complete all-simplex target; hidden older convex-geometric equivalence remains a material residual risk.
residual_risks: An older source may state the general homothetic erosion of a simplex by a convex set, making the present equality a short corollary of known width optimization; search does not rule this out.
The balanced-partition regular-simplex minimizer classification was already known by 2023 (and cited sources even earlier).
The Gritzmann–Klee full paper and older Alexander 1977 were not materially read; the abstracts/title are not evidence of noncoverage.
Resultary search absence cannot itself establish priority; human expert historical search remains useful.

value.rationale: The new exact identity evaluates the directional geometric quantity left open after the key Corollary 7 reduction of an active quantitative plank problem. It proves that every nondegenerate simplex, including regular tetrahedra outside the older altitude-equality class, reaches the Bang homothetic lower bound at the erosion stage and identifies every complementary-face direction doing so. This is a natural infinite-dimensional-family structural lemma and usefully isolates the unsolved step from optimized erosion to actual one-plank uncovered volume. The simplex barycentric computation and standard width polarity are elementary, and the regular-width balanced-partition corollary is known; mathematical value belongs only to the complete all-simplex sharp erosion formula for the partial-plank reduction, not to those routine sublemmas.
residual_risks: The result does not settle the higher-dimensional single-plank conjecture, so its value is as a sharp reduction-stage lemma only.
An older all-simplex erosion formula would substantially diminish originality and value; older literature search is not exhaustive.
No new general inequality for non-simplices is asserted.
